The image presents two line charts, each displaying various economic indicators over time. The x-axis for both charts represents the years from 1995 to 2020, with a linear scale and tick labels at five-year intervals.

The left chart features three lines: a blue line representing an unspecified metric, a purple line indicating the "Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat" (total government debt ratio), and a series of blue and red triangles denoting the "IWF Fiskalindex" (IMF fiscal index). The y-axis on the left side of the chart measures the unspecified metric and the total government debt ratio, ranging from 0 to 2.5 and 60 to 120, respectively. The blue line starts at approximately 0.1 in 1995, increases to around 1 in 2008, and then decreases to about 0.25 in 2019 before rising to 0.5 in 2020. The purple line begins at roughly 60 in 1995, peaks at 100 in 2015, and reaches 110 in 2020. The IWF Fiskalindex remains relatively stable, with blue triangles indicating values around 1 and red triangles showing values around 0.5.

The right chart also displays three lines: a blue line representing an unspecified metric, a purple line indicating the "Schuldenquote Zentralstaat" (central government debt ratio), and a series of blue and red triangles denoting the "IWF Fiskalindex" (IMF fiscal index). The y-axis on the right side of the chart measures the unspecified metric and the central government debt ratio, ranging from -5 to 2 and 30 to 70, respectively. The blue line starts at around -1 in 1995, increases to approximately 0.5 in 2008, and then fluctuates before rising to 1 in 2020. The purple line begins at roughly 35 in 1995, peaks at 50 in 2010, and reaches 60 in 2020. The IWF Fiskalindex remains relatively stable, with blue triangles indicating values around 1 and red triangles showing values around 0.5.

Both charts illustrate the trends and fluctuations in these economic indicators over the specified time period.
